meta.title: Ranch — floor plan, 3D walk, photos and history
meta.description: Floor plan, a walkable 3D model, the listing photos and the history of a former guesthouse in La Cumbre, Córdoba.
intro.kicker: López y Planes 132 · La Cumbre, Córdoba
intro.title: Ranch
intro.lede: A former guesthouse on a 765 m² lot: the main house on the street, a wing of guest rooms along the garden and an independent apartment over the covered drive. Rooms and walls follow the survey plan drawn in 2015; furniture and finishes come from the 54 listing photos, two walkthrough videos and our visit. The survey is a hand-measured drawing, not a building permit, so check sizes on site.

walk.note: Walls, doors and rooms follow the 2015 survey plan; heights, finishes and furniture follow the photos and videos, so treat it as a sketch. The neighbours' buildings are blocks drawn from the cadastre, each the size of its built area. Doors start closed: click one to open it. A click on the little map takes you there. There are stairs up to the apartment, behind its red street door, and to the wing's roof, from the grill.
facts.title: What the listings and records say
facts.intro: Everything we found about the house at López y Planes 132, La Cumbre (some directories write 1332).
facts.cadastre.title: Cadastre — Córdoba provincial register (IDECOR)
facts.cadastre.01: Parcel 053 in block 059 (nomenclature 23-01-29-11-04-059-053), lot 2 of plan 0033-072122/2003; registered as built, not a PH unit.
facts.cadastre.02: Land 765 m² and buildings 414 m², the same figures as the sale listing.
facts.cadastre.03: About 20.1 m of frontage on the west side of López y Planes, between Tucumán and Rivadavia; 36.7 m along the north side, 38.8 m along the south side, 19.7 m across the back.
facts.cadastre.04: 2026 fiscal valuation: ARS 164 million (land 52.4 M, buildings 111.6 M).
facts.sale.title: Sale listing — Links Propiedades, ref. 0336 (also on Zonaprop)
facts.sale.01: USD 180,000; two floors. The listing calls it about 50 years old, but the survey dates the oldest part to 1930.
facts.sale.02: Guesthouse half a block from the center: 4 rooms each with a private bath, sitting room, galería, kitchen, grill, laundry, garden, parking and a SUM. Zonaprop calls it 6 en-suite bedrooms.
facts.sale.03: Independent first-floor apartment: 1 bedroom en suite, 2 baths, kitchen, living-dining, views of the sierras. Natural gas connected.
facts.sale.04: The counts disagree: the agency says 6 bedrooms, 6 baths and 5 parking spaces; Zonaprop says 8 rooms, 6 bedrooms, 5 baths and 1 semi-covered garage.
facts.rental.title: Rental listing — AlquilerArgentina (ph44)
facts.rental.01: Rented as two units: the house (up to 13 guests, 4 bedrooms, 4 baths) and the first-floor apartment (up to 5 guests, 1 bedroom, 2 baths).
facts.rental.02: Lists park, parking, grill, TV, heating and kitchen; pets allowed; marked suitable for people with reduced mobility.
facts.photos.title: What the photos, the satellite and Street View show
facts.photos.01: The house is built on the sidewalk line. From the north: the vehicle gate under the apartment, the apartment's red door, two big windows, the main entrance (a double glass door), the bedroom window over a stone base.
facts.photos.02: Covered drive along the north side; two paver tracks cross the lawn to an L-shaped carport at the back.
facts.photos.03: Guest wing along the south side: a galería with a wooden railing and the rooms' doors, a flat roof with a decorative railing and a small storeroom with the water tank. Grill at its end, with a steel stair up to the roof.
facts.photos.04: Glazed reception and breakfast room with a barrel-vault roof; dining room with a black-and-white checkerboard floor; a long sitting room with rattan furniture; the main kitchen.
facts.photos.05: At least five different guest bedrooms (most with two or three single beds, one with a double) and five or more bathrooms.
facts.photos.06: Apartment: inside stair, bedroom with a sliding door to the street balcony, living-dining with a garden balcony, small kitchen with windows on two sides, two bathrooms.

history.lede: What we could find about the house and the town around it: public records, the listings and fifteen years of guest reviews.
history.time.title: Timeline
history.time.01: The land where La Cumbre stands is granted as part of the San Gerónimo estancia.
history.time.02: The Córdoba–Cruz del Eje railway is finished; a village grows around the station, nine minutes' walk from the house.
history.time.03: The station, until then San Gerónimo, opens its first summer timetable as La Cumbre.
history.time.04: British railway families and summer visitors build the town; the golf club is founded in 1924. The street is named after Vicente López y Planes, who wrote the words of the national anthem.
history.time.05: The 8 m Cristo Redentor goes up on cerro La Viarapa; it can be seen from the garden.
history.time.06: The oldest part of the house (A on the survey) is built; the town has records of it.
history.time.08: A survey plan gives the lot its present outline as lot 2 (765 m²); the plot behind it, lot 5, comes from the same plan.
history.time.09: It is running as Hostería Norita Ranch, two stars: a guest who first stayed that year kept coming back.
history.time.10: Eight Tripadvisor reviews give it 4.5 out of 5.
history.time.11: The newest part (C) goes up, and in August 2015 a survey plan puts 486 m² of buildings on record.
history.time.12: Rented as two units: the house for up to 13 guests and the upstairs apartment for 5. The agency's photos date from October.
history.owners.title: Who owned it
history.owners.01: The guesthouse took its name from its owner, Nora, “Norita” to her guests, who ran it herself; the 2015 survey is in her name. Reviews from 2006 to 2019 speak of her more than of the rooms.
history.owners.02: Nora has since died, and her heirs are selling. This is their second try: the first fell through because some documents were missing; we are told they are now all in order. From about 2021 the house was let as two units through a rental site, and it is sold through Links Propiedades in La Cumbre (ref. 0336).
history.owners.03: The current registered owner is not public. The title report (informe de dominio) from the Registro General de la Provincia says who signs; the escribano asks for it, with the tax account 230124740024, before the deed.
history.reviews.title: What guests said
history.meters.title: Tripadvisor, by topic (out of 5)
history.liked.title: What they liked
history.liked.01: Quiet and homely: “like being at home” is the most common line, and a guest who returned again and again since 2006 called it “a place to stay and live”.
history.liked.02: The big, well-kept garden with tables and armchairs, and the Cristo on the hill seen from it.
history.liked.03: The shared rooms: the winter garden (the glazed room), the dining room and the sitting room, all furnished for guests.
history.liked.04: Rooms inside the main house plus two or three with their own door to the garden, “like small one-room flats”; small pets welcome.
history.liked.05: Covered parking, and the center three blocks away, all on foot.
history.disliked.title: What they didn't
history.disliked.01: One 2018 stay: old mattresses, thin pillows, a small TV on a wardrobe and a tiny bathroom whose door didn't close.
history.disliked.02: Some bedrooms felt small, and one guest thought the price didn't match the place.
history.disliked.03: No breakfast as a rule (it could be arranged), and house rules posted everywhere.
history.area.title: Around the house
history.area.01: A few blocks from the center: 27 restaurants within 500 m, and the bus terminal seven minutes' walk away.
history.area.02: The town hospital, Hospital Municipal Dr. Oscar Vignaroli, is at López y Planes 65, about 80 m away across the street.
history.area.03: The railway station, nine minutes' walk; the Cristo Redentor about a kilometer.
history.area.04: Hostería San Martín, a few doors along at number 174, has taken guests since 1923: the street has long been one of guesthouses.
history.area.05: La Cumbre sits at about 1,140 m in the Punilla valley and had 7,200 people in the 2022 census.
facts.cadastre.05: Provincial tax account 230124740024; the parcel was created by survey plan 0033-072122/2003 in October 2003.

facts.survey.title: Survey plan — August 2015
facts.survey.01: A “plano de transcripción y relevamiento” at 1:100, drawn to put the built area on record: block 059, parcel 050 (now 053), lot 2, zone Z1.
facts.survey.02: Land 765.50 m². Covered: 141.00 m² already registered plus 229.22 m² surveyed; semi-covered 115.75 m²; 485.97 m² in all.
facts.survey.03: Ages: the parts marked A date from 1930, with municipal records; B from 2000; C were about a year old (2014).
facts.survey.04: It states that what it declares was built without a professional's supervision: worth asking whether this plan was approved by the municipality.
facts.survey.05: Zone Z1 allows FOS 0.80 and FOT 1.00; the house uses 0.52 and 0.62. The street is 12 m wide and paved, with 2.50 m sidewalks.
history.time.13: For sale at USD 180,000 (Links Propiedades, also on Zonaprop), the heirs' second try. The apartment still gets a five-star Google review in September.
